text: The committee's findings, though cautious, admit of only one reading: the scheme was abandoned not for want of money but for want of nerve. Its architects had underestimated, from the outset, the resistance of the parishes; they had assumed that a rational plan, once published, would recommend itself. It did not. By the spring of the following year the surveyors had been withdrawn, the ledgers closed, and the whole affair consigned to that peculiar silence in which institutions bury their embarrassments. What remains is a question of judgement rather than of fact.
